artifacts.description:
The distribution of mobility points density (per km²) across the area’s administrative sub-areas, shown as a box plot (median, quartiles and outliers). A long tail or low median points to many under-served neighbourhoods.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Statistics
artifacts.summary: Spread, inequality and clustering measures for the area’s mobility points. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.18. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of mobility points density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over mobility points density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Public-transport access score
artifacts.summary: A combined layer (weighted sum) of 3×Train stations & halts, 2.5×Metro & subway stations, 2×Tram & light-rail stops, 1×Bus stops, 1×Bike-sharing points, 0.5×Car-sharing points, per sub-area. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Map algebra: for each administrative sub-area, the per-km² densities of the input categories are combined by **weighted sum** — 3×Train stations & halts, 2.5×Metro & subway stations, 2×Tram & light-rail stops, 1×Bus stops, 1×Bike-sharing points, 0.5×Car-sharing points — into a single value. Use it to express a composite index (e.g. a weighted suitability score) as one layer instead of several.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Density by sub-area
artifacts.summary: Mobility points density (per km²) across the neighbourhoods of the area. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into OpenStreetMap administrative sub-areas, each shaded by its mobility points density (per km²). Use it to compare how well different neighbourhoods are served.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Sub-area ranking
artifacts.summary: Neighbourhoods ranked by mobility points density (per km²). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Mobility points density per km² for each administrative sub-area, ordered from highest to lowest.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Top sub-areas
artifacts.summary: The 10 best-served neighbourhoods by mobility points density (per km²). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The 10 administrative sub-areas with the highest mobility points density, with their count, area and density — a compact, sortable companion to the ranking chart.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do mobility points track where people live? Mobility points per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its mobility points per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Mobility points per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of mobility points per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Coverage on foot
artifacts.summary: About 80% of the area is within 300 m on foot of a mobility point. About 99% of residents are within reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into the part within reach (on foot) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Underserved areas
artifacts.summary: Share of each neighbourhood beyond 300 m on foot of any mobility point. About 479 residents live beyond that reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by the fraction of its area that lies **beyond reach** (on foot) of any feature — the complement of the coverage map. Darker = more underserved. Use it to target where new provision would reach the most currently-unserved people.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Most underserved sub-areas
artifacts.summary: The 10 neighbourhoods with the largest share beyond 300 m on foot of a mobility point. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The 10 administrative sub-areas with the greatest share of their area beyond reach (on foot) of any feature — a sortable companion to the underserved-areas map.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Mobility points heatmap
artifacts.summary: A gridded density of mobility points across the area — brighter means more. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many mobility points fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Mobility points density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of mobility points (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of mobility points: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest mobility point
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest mobility point from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest mobility point. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each mobility point was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 1 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: mobility_points · reachability: straight-line distance.
